samples: This module reads a service's JSON configuration file and checks that it has a valid port (1 to 65535), a worker count (1 to 64) and a log level of quiet, normal or verbose. If the file can't be read or doesn't match that shape, it fails with an error saying which problem occurred. It also offers built-in defaults and a loader that falls back to a configuration you supply when loading fails, while an older fallback-to-defaults loader is deprecated in favor of that one.

This module reads a service's JSON configuration file and checks it against a fixed shape: a port between 1 and 65535, a worker count between 1 and 64, and a log level of quiet, normal, or verbose. Loading reports a distinct error when the file cannot be read and another when its contents don't match that shape, and there is also a built-in default configuration (port 8080, four workers, normal logging). If you want a fallback when loading fails, use the fallback-taking loader, since the older load-or-default function is deprecated since version 0.2.

This module reads a JSON service configuration file (port, worker count, and log level) and checks that the port is within 1–65535 and workers within 1–64, failing with a clear error if the file is unreadable or doesn't match. It also offers a built-in default configuration (port 8080, 4 workers, normal logging) and a loader that falls back to a configuration you supply when loading fails. The older "load or default" function is deprecated in favor of the fallback version, so new code should use that one.

This module reads a service's JSON configuration file and checks that it has a valid port (1 to 65535), a worker count (1 to 64) and a log level of quiet, normal or verbose. If the file can't be read or doesn't match that shape, loading fails with an error that says which problem occurred. It also provides built-in defaults (port 8080, 4 workers, normal logging) and a loader that falls back to a configuration you supply, while the older default-fallback loader is deprecated in favor of that one.

This module reads a JSON configuration file for a service and checks that it has a valid port (1 to 65535), a worker count (1 to 64), and a log level of quiet, normal or verbose, reporting either an unreadable file or an invalid shape as the failure. It also offers built-in defaults (port 8080, 4 workers, normal logging) and a loader that falls back to a configuration you supply when the file can't be loaded. The only permission it needs is reading files, and you should use the fallback loader rather than the older default-only one, which is deprecated.
